questions.question: Virat can complete a work in 30 days and Daniel is 60% more efficient than Virat to complete the same work. Find the total time taken by Daniel to complete the work.
questions.solution:
Given

Daniel is 60% more efficient than Virat.

Virat can complete a work in 30 days.

Concept

Efficiency is inversely related to time.

Work done = efficiency × time

Calculation

Let the efficiency of Virat is 100

So, the efficiency of Daniel is 160

The ratio of efficiency, Virat: Daniel = 100: 160

⇒ 5 : 8

It is inversely related to time

Ratio of time = 8 : 5

8 : 5 = 30 : x

So, 8 → 30 days

then

1 → 30/8 days

⇒ 5 = x → 150/8 days

= 75/4 = 18(3/4) days

**Daniel can complete a work in 18(3/4) days.**

questions.question: If sin 23° = (a)/(b), then the value of sec 23° - sin 67° is __________.
questions.solution:
Given:

sin 23° = a/b

Concepts used:

In a right-angled triangle, applying Pythagoras Theorem,

H² = P² + B²

⇒ P² = H² – B²

P → Perpendicular, B → base, H → Hypotenuse of right-angled triangle

sinθ = P/H

cosθ = B/H

tanθ = P/B

Calculation:

sin23° = P/H = a/b

On comparing,

⇒ P = a units and H = b units

Using Pythagoras' Theorem,

⇒ B² = H² – P²

⇒ B² = b² – a²

⇒ B = √b2 – a2

⇒ sec23° = H/B = b/√b2 – a2

⇒ Cos23° = sin67° = √b2 – a2 /b

sec 23° - sin 67° ⇒ b/√b2 – a² - √b2 – a2 /b

sec 23° - sin 67° ⇒ (a²)/(b sqrt{b²-a²)}

**The value is (a²)/(b sqrt{b²-a²)}**

questions.question: In an election between three candidates, Arjun, Bhaskar and Saral contested for a post. Arjun got 50% votes more than Saral, and Saral got 2% votes less than Bhaskar. The difference between the votes of Bhaskar and Saral is 1296. What is the half of the difference between the votes of Arjun and Bhaskar?
questions.solution:
Given:

Arjun got 50% votes more than Saral, and Saral got 2% votes less than Bhaskar.

The difference between the votes of Bhaskar and Saral = 1296

Formula used:

Percentage = (Part / Whole) × 100

Solution:

Let the total number of votes Bhaskar got be 100x.

The votes received by Saral = 100x - 2% of 100x

⇒ 98x

The votes received by Arjun = 98x + 50% of 98x

⇒ 147x

The difference between the votes of Bhaskar and Saral = 1296

⇒ 100x - 98x = 1296

⇒ x = 1296/2

⇒ x = 648

The difference between the votes of Bhaskar and Arjun = 147x - 100x

⇒ 47x

Half of the difference between the votes of Arjun and Bhaskar = 47x/2

⇒ x → 648

⇒ 47x/2 → 648 × 47/2

⇒ 47x/2 → 324 × 47

⇒ 47x/2 → 15228

**Half of the difference between the votes of Arjun and Bhaskar is 15228.**

questions.question: Two friends P and Q simultaneously start running from same point around a circular track. They run in the same direction. P runs at 6 m/sec and Q runs at b m/sec. If they cross each other at exactly two points on the circular track and b is a natural number less than 6, then how many values can b take?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P runs at 6 m/sec and Q runs at b m/sec.

they cross each other at exactly two points on the circular track and b is a natural number less than 6.

**Formula used**

Time = Distance/relative speed

When running in the same direction, relative speed = a - b.

**Calculation**

Let track length be equal to T.

Time taken to meet for the first time = T/(6 - b)

questions.question: A dealer professing to sell his goods at cost price uses 950 grams weight for 1 kg. His gain percentage is: (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
**Given**

A dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price uses 950 grams weight for 1 kg.

Formula used

Profit = SP - CP

% profit = (profit /CP) × 100

Calculation

Let the CP of 1 g = x

Given CP of 1 kg = SP of 1 kg = 1000x

But the CP of what he is selling = 950x

His Profit = 1000x – 950x = 50x

% Profit = (50x/950x) × 100 = 5(1/19)

∴ The required profit% is 5.26%.

questions.question: A trader allows a 20% trade discount and a 30% cash discount. If the list price is Rs. 1,200, then the selling price (in Rs.) is:

Trade discount = 20%

Cash discount = 30% 

Concept used:

M.P. = S.P. × 100/(100 – discount %)

Calculation:

Trader provides 20% trade discount and 30% cash discount on the list price.

The list price = Rs. 1200

∴ The selling price = Rs. 1200 × (80/100) × (70/100) 

= Rs. 672

**The selling price is Rs. 672.**

questions.question: If x + (1)/(x) = 7, then the value of x⁶ + (1)/(x⁶) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

x + 1/x = 7

Formula used:

If x + 1/x = n

then, x ² + 1/x² = n² - 2

And (x³ + y³) = n³ - 3n

Calculation:

x + 1/x = 7

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 7² - 2

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 47

Cubing both side we get

⇒ (x2 + 1/x2)³ = 47³

⇒ x⁶ + 1/x⁶ + 3 (x2 × 1/x2) (x2 + 1/x2) = 47³ 

⇒ x6 + 1/x6 + 3 × 1 × 47 = 473 

⇒ x6 + 1/x6 = 473 - 3 × 47

⇒ x 6 + 1/x 6 = 103823 - 141

⇒ x 6 + 1/x 6 = 103682

∴ The value of x 6 + 1/x 6 is 103682.

questions.question: The current ages of Sudhir and Ashish are in the ratio 5 ∶ 7. Twelve years ago, the ratio of their ages was 1 ∶ 2. What will be the age of Sudhir after five years from now?

questions.question: A man invests a total sum of Rs. 10,000 in a company. A part of the sum was invested at 10% simple interest per annum and the remaining part at 15% simple interest per annum. If the total interest accrued to him in two years equals Rs. 2,400, the sum invested at 15% simple interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs 10,000

Some part of money lent at 15%

Some part of it lent at 10%

Total interest earned = Rs. 2400

Time = 2 years

Formula Used:

Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

Calculation:

Let the money lent at 15% be x

Then money lent at 10% be (10,000 - x)

2400 = [(x × 15 × 2)/100] + [(10,000 - x) × 10 × 2]/100

⇒ 2400 = (3x/10) + [(10,000 - x)/5]

⇒ 2400 = (3x + 20,000 - 2x)/10

⇒ 24,000 = 20,000 + x

⇒ x = Rs 4,000

**The sum invested at 15% simple interest per annum is 4000.**

questions.question: Jehangir had to cover a distance of 90 km in an hour. During the first 25 minutes he travelled at a speed of 15.2 metres per second. How many metres did Jehangir cover per second during the remaining period to reach his destination just on time?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Total distance = 90 km = 90000 metres

Total time = 1 hour = 3600 seconds

Time spent travelling at 15.2 m/s = 25 minutes = 1500 seconds

Speed during first 25 minutes = 15.2 m/s

 

**Concept to be used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

Distance covered in first 25 minutes = Speed × Time

⇒ 15.2 m/s × 1500 s = 22800 metres

Remaining distance to be covered = Total distance - Distance covered in first 25 min

⇒ 90000 m - 22800 m = 67200 metres

Remaining time = Total time - Time spent in first 25 min

⇒ 3600 s - 1500 s = 2100 seconds

Speed during remaining time = Remaining distance / Remaining time

⇒ 67200 m / 2100 s = 32 m/s

**Therefore, Jehangir should travel at a speed of 32 m/s for the remaining time to reach his destination on time.**
